stemMd: Which statement would the curator most likely accept?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A conservation decision can preserve some values while altering others

options.label: B
options.textMd: Only untouched buildings have any historical value

options.label: C
options.textMd: Access concerns are irrelevant to conservation

options.label: D
options.textMd: Explaining a change is the same as denying it occurred

options.label: E
options.textMd: A retained object guarantees an unchanged historical experience

explanationMd: The curator acknowledges the survival of material and documentation alongside a change in use. This supports a selective, explicit understanding of preservation. It does not claim that intervention either saves everything or destroys all value.

distractorRationale.e: The passage directly rejects that guarantee.
distractorRationale.c: The near-fall problem is a major reason for intervention.
distractorRationale.b: The museum continues interpreting the altered building.
distractorRationale.d: The display openly acknowledges the change.
